clue.text: German volume with article by Scots writer

parts.note: Buch is the German word for a book or volume
an is the indefinite article

explanation.surface: A German tome comes with a piece contributed by a Scottish author.
explanation.walkthrough: John Buchan, author of The Thirty-Nine Steps, was a Scot; 'with' and 'by' are link words.
explanation.definitionFit: John Buchan was a Scottish novelist and statesman, so he is a Scots writer.

clue.text: The real LBJ needed protective covering

indicators.note: needed sounds like kneaded, and kneaded letters are worked into a new shape

explanation.surface: President Johnson, the genuine article, required some shielding.
explanation.walkthrough: 'needed' is a pun on 'kneaded': the letters of REAL LBJ are worked like dough. 'The' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: A bell jar is a glass dome placed over delicate objects or plants to shield them.

clue.text: Standard that shall be (more or less) nameless

parts.note: c, short for circa, means approximately
anon, short for anonymous, means nameless

explanation.surface: A benchmark set by someone who, more or less, must not be named.
explanation.walkthrough: 'that shall be' completes the phrase 'who shall be nameless' and is a link; C (circa) means roughly.
explanation.definitionFit: A canon is an accepted rule or criterion, a standard by which things are judged.

clue.text: A temple largely by instinct given to anti-multiculturalism

indicators.note: only the greater part of the temple's name is used, its last letters cut off

parts.note: the Parthenon is the great temple on the Athenian Acropolis
the id is the instinctive part of the psyche in Freudian theory

explanation.surface: An ancient temple seems to be driven by gut feeling towards opposing cultural mixing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'largely' removes NON from PARTHENON, leaving PARTHE; 'by' and 'given to' are link words.
explanation.definitionFit: Apartheid was South Africa's system of enforced racial separation, the opposite of a multicultural society.

clue.text: Defence against batterer — retreating trap

parts.note: a ram, or battering ram, batters down walls and gates

indicators.note: retreating means going backwards, so the word trap is read in reverse

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A fortification protects against an attacker as a snare is withdrawn.
explanation.walkthrough: 'against' is a link word in its sense of 'next to'; the batterer is the battering ram, not a person.
explanation.definitionFit: A rampart is a defensive wall or bank surrounding a fort.

clue.text: Holey things the oracle spoke in

definitions.meaning: oracles gave answers as puzzles or enigmas

explanation.definitionFit: A riddle is both a coarse sieve and an enigmatic puzzle, the form oracles favoured.

clue.text: Complaint that is ma and pa's initially

parts.note: ma is a familiar word for mother, mum
the initials of pa and of the 's are P and S

explanation.surface: An illness that, at first, both mother and father have.
explanation.walkthrough: 'that is' and 'and' are link words; 'initially' takes the first letters of pa and its 's.
explanation.definitionFit: Mumps is a viral illness, and complaint is an everyday word for an ailment.

clue.text: Deviser of the melting of the Arctic

indicators.note: melting breaks down the Arctic's form, so its letters lose their shape and reform

explanation.surface: Someone responsible for the polar ice melting away.
explanation.walkthrough: 'melting of' scrambles THE ARCTIC.
explanation.definitionFit: An architect is one who designs or devises something, as in 'the architect of the plan'.

clue.text: Tool brought up from the Shuttleworth collection

indicators.note: in a down clue brought up means read from bottom to top, backwards
from signals that the letters are taken out of the name that follows

explanation.surface: An implement lifted from a museum's holdings.
explanation.walkthrough: LEWORT sits inside ShuttLEWORTh and 'brought up' reverses it. The Shuttleworth Collection is an aviation and vehicle museum in Bedfordshire; 'collection' completes the name and is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A trowel is a small hand tool used by gardeners and bricklayers.

clue.text: A politician in a little trap for wasps?

indicators.note: in places A and the politician inside the word for a little

parts.note: a jot is a very small amount
MP stands for Member of Parliament

explanation.surface: An MP is caught in a small snare set for insects.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark marks the definition as a description by example: a jam pot is not made as a trap, but serves as one.
explanation.definitionFit: A jam pot left out attracts wasps, which crawl in and drown, so it works as a wasp trap.

clue.text: Back Prince grasps purpose with help

indicators.note: grasps means holds, so one piece is held inside another
back signals the prince's name is written backwards

parts.note: Prince Hal is Shakespeare's young Henry V
an end is an aim or purpose
and means along with

explanation.surface: A prince supports a goal with assistance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Back' turns HAL into LAH, which 'grasps' END to give LENDAH.
explanation.definitionFit: To lend a hand is an idiom meaning to give help.

clue.text: Flier defying logic with mirth

indicators.note: letters that defy their order break out of it and rearrange

explanation.surface: Something airborne that defies reason with laughter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'defying' rearranges LOGIC and MIRTH together; 'with' joins them.
explanation.definitionFit: A microlight is a very small, light aircraft, so it is a flier.

clue.text: Flier holding a name for a girl

indicators.note: holding means one piece contains the other

parts.note: a jet is an aircraft, something that flies

explanation.surface: An aircraft named after a girl.
explanation.walkthrough: 'holding' puts A N inside JET; 'for' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: Janet is a common female first name, so it can stand for a girl, the definition by example.

clue.text: Limits sticker for holy land

parts.note: pales are boundaries, as in 'beyond the pale'
a tine is a prong that sticks into things

explanation.surface: Borders that stick, around a sacred territory.
explanation.walkthrough: 'for' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: Palestine is the historic region of the Bible, known as the Holy Land.

clue.text: Think how to bounce back?

definitions.meaning: a mirror sends light back by reflection

explanation.definitionFit: To reflect means both to ponder and to throw back light or sound from a surface.

clue.text: Best method of frater aid?

indicators.note: a method is a way of arranging things, so the letters are put in a new order

explanation.surface: The ideal way to give brotherly help.
explanation.walkthrough: A frater is a brother (Latin), so 'frater aid' is brotherly help; 'method of' rearranges FRATER AID.
explanation.definitionFit: Fair trade is an ethical trading system that pays producers fairly, a fraternal way of aiding them.

clue.text: Assembly due to accept the lovesick's report

indicators.note: accept means take in, so one piece goes inside another

parts.note: set means due or scheduled, as in 'set to arrive'
lovesick said aloud sounds like love six, which is O and VI

explanation.surface: A gathering is about to take in someone pining for love.
explanation.walkthrough: Love is O (zero) and six is VI; 'report' says lovesick sounds like 'love six'. 'to' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: A soviet was an elected council or assembly in the USSR.

clue.text: Island city takes a turn in the front cover

parts.note: the van is the front of an army or procession

indicators.note: in places the turn inside the cover

parts.note: taken as written
a U-turn, or U, is a turn

explanation.surface: A city on an island takes a twist inside the front cover.
explanation.walkthrough: 'takes' and 'the' are link words.
explanation.definitionFit: Vancouver is a Canadian city and Vancouver Island lies just off it, so both senses share the name.

clue.text: The leg-pulling church, down (to the Wyre?), but still independent

definitions.text: down (to the Wyre?), but still independent

parts.note: a kidder is one who pulls people's legs, a teaser
a minster is a large church

explanation.surface: A joking church is down by the Wyre but still independent.
explanation.walkthrough: Kidderminster is a town in the Wyre Forest district; when its hospital was run down, an Independent MP was elected there in 2001.
explanation.definitionFit: Kidderminster, in the Wyre Forest, lost its hospital yet returned an Independent MP, fitting this description.

clue.text: Corruption providing the Queen with an invisible revolutionary

parts.note: rot means decay or corruption
if means provided that
ER stands for Elizabeth Regina

explanation.surface: Rot, provided the monarch stands beside an unseen rebel.
explanation.walkthrough: A rotifer is a microscopic water animal with rings of beating hairs that look like turning wheels, hence 'revolutionary'.
explanation.definitionFit: Rotifers are too small to see without a microscope and their cilia appear to rotate like wheels.

clue.text: See 17
A month on the border causing havoc

parts.note: May is a month of the year
a hem is the edge or border of a garment

explanation.surface: A month on the frontier brings chaos.
explanation.walkthrough: 'causing' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: Mayhem is violent disorder, a synonym of havoc.

clue.text: Beast perused expensive reports

indicators.note: reports signals words spoken out loud, so the answer sounds like them

parts.note: perused means read, and expensive means dear

explanation.surface: An animal studied costly accounts.
explanation.walkthrough: READ (past tense) sounds like RED and DEAR like DEER.
explanation.definitionFit: The red deer is a large wild animal, a beast of the British countryside.

clue.text: University river with Manx cat?

parts.note: the Cam is the river through Cambridge

indicators.note: a Manx cat has no tail, so the word for cat loses its last letter

parts.note: puss is a word for a cat

explanation.surface: A university by the river with a tailless cat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'with' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: A campus is the grounds of a university, standing for the university itself.

clue.text: Learner has a go chasing a car — excessive sense of self-worth?

indicators.note: chasing means following behind, so these pieces come after the car

parts.note: auto is short for automobile, a car
L is a learner driver's plate
a go is an attempt, a try

explanation.surface: A learner driver has a go at chasing a car, perhaps from vanity.
explanation.walkthrough: 'has' and the 'a' before car are link words.
explanation.definitionFit: Autolatry is self-worship, which suggests an inflated sense of one's own worth.

clue.text: See 10
Not squeaking under the influence?

definitions.meaning: a hinge with oil on it no longer squeaks

explanation.definitionFit: Oiled means both lubricated so as not to squeak and, colloquially, drunk.

clue.text: Left Christian grouping at hospital — no place to be left in!

definitions.text: no place to be left in!

parts.note: URC is the United Reformed Church
H is the map abbreviation for hospital

explanation.surface: A left-wing Christian group at the hospital: a terrible place to be abandoned.
explanation.walkthrough: 'at' is a link word; to be 'left in the lurch' is to be abandoned in difficulty.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom 'left in the lurch' means abandoned when in trouble, so it is nowhere to be left.

clue.text: Flier's problem: its leader requested service

parts.note: the leader of the word problem is its first letter, P
someone who rang a bell asked to be served

explanation.surface: A pilot's trouble: the chief summoned attention.
explanation.walkthrough: 'its' refers back to 'problem'. A prang is British slang for a crash.
explanation.definitionFit: A prang is a crash or collision, a problem for any pilot.

clue.text: Female magistrate rebelled without love, writing unruled lines

parts.note: a reeve was a local magistrate or official

indicators.note: without means lacking, so the letter for love is removed

parts.note: rose, as in rose up, means rebelled
love is zero in tennis, O

explanation.surface: A woman magistrate rebelled, loveless, and wrote poetry without rules.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' takes O from ROSE, leaving RSE.
explanation.definitionFit: Free verse is poetry without regular metre or rhyme, lines not ruled by form.

clue.text: Jumper showing signs of exertion?

definitions.meaning: a jumper is a knitted pullover

explanation.definitionFit: A sweater is a knitted pullover, and literally one who sweats from effort.

clue.text: King painting Ben Hur's father?

parts.note: painting is a form of art
ben means son of in Hebrew, so Ben Hur's father is Hur

explanation.surface: A monarch depicts the father of the hero Ben Hur.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ben' in a Hebrew name means 'son of', so the father of Ben Hur would be Hur.
explanation.definitionFit: Arthur is the legendary King of Britain.
